title: State of Buenos Aires
capsule: The State of Buenos Aires (Estado de Buenos Aires) was a breakaway Argentine republic established on 11 September 1852 when Buenos Aires province refused to ratify the San Nicolás Agreement that would have given Justo José de Urquiza's Argentine Confederation access to the port and its customs revenues. Under its own constitution (1854) the State conducted independent foreign policy, issued currency, and launched Argentina's first railway on 30 August 1857. The Confederation defeated Buenos Aires at the Battle of Cepeda (23 October 1859) and imposed the Pacto de San José de Flores, but Buenos Aires Governor Bartolomé Mitre defeated Urquiza at the Battle of Pavón (17 September 1861), after which Buenos Aires rejoined and effectively assumed leadership of a reunified Argentina.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The State of Buenos Aires corresponded to Buenos Aires Province and is well-bounded by documented administrative records; its de facto jurisdiction is clearly delimited by the contemporary Confederation boundary.
